raw:
These hypotheses rest on prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201, not on results from the 100 experiments, which are unavailable. The main mechanism is connectivity. Edges 3 (0->3), 4 (1->3) and 5 (2->3) feed the output, and conv ops on a path matter much more when the alternative paths are weak or absent. Edits that add a conv to an otherwise disconnected or thin cell should gain the most.

1. Setting edge 5 to nor_conv_3x3 gains more when edge 5 is currently none than when it is skip_connect. Going from none to conv adds a path, while skip to conv is only an upgrade.
2. Setting edge 3 to skip_connect is higher when edge 3 is currently none, because adding a skip path to the output stabilizes training, whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity.
3. Setting edge 0 to nor_conv_3x3 is higher when edge 0 is currently none, since that connects the input to the rest of the cell. Replacing a skip or pool is a smaller gain.
4. Setting edge 2 to none is lower when edge 3 is skip_connect than when edge 3 is none. The 0->3 skip path already provides a shortcut, so the removal costs little. Hence this is a "higher" effect, since the edit hurts less. I state it as higher.
5. Setting edge 4 to none is lower when edge 3 is none, because removing edge 4 then leaves fewer paths to the output.
6. Setting edge 1 to none is higher (less harmful) when edge 2 is none, because edge 1 then has no downstream path through node 2.
7. Setting edge 3 to none is lower when edge 3 is currently nor_conv_3x3 than when it is skip_connect, because removing a conv costs more than removing a skip.
8. Setting edge 5 to nor_conv_3x3 is higher when edge 5 is currently none than when it is avg_pool_3x3, because none-to-conv adds a path.
9. Setting edge 3 to nor_conv_3x3 is higher when edge 3 is currently none, because it adds a direct conv path to the output.
10. Setting edge 0 to none is lower when edge 1 is none, because edge 0 then carries the only path to node 1 or node 2 and removing it hurts more.
